author: Jenna Lejano
title: Portsmouth Health Department to launch PATH harm reduction site in 2026 - NewsBreak
text:
By Jenna Lejano No media credit provided. ,
8 hours ago
PORTSMOUTH, Va. (WAVY) — The Portsmouth Health Department will hold a grand opening for a new comprehensive harm reduction site, PATH: Portsmouth Access to Harm Reduction, on Thursday, April 9, 2026, according to a press release.
PATH: Portsmouth Access to Harm Reduction Grand Opening
Thursday, April 9, 2026, 10 a.m.- 11 a.m. Portsmouth Health Department, 1701 High Street, Suite 102, Portsmouth, Va. 23704 The new site is dedicated to reducing the spread of infectious diseases, preventing overdose deaths, and connecting individuals to essential health and social services.
This initiative is part of an evidence-based statewide effort by the Virginia Department of Health to improve health outcomes for people who use drugs and to promote a safer, healthier community.
“PATH reflects our commitment to meeting people where they are with compassion, dignity, and practical support,” said Angela Tillery, acting Portsmouth Health Director. “By offering evidence-based harm reduction services, we can save lives and strengthen the overall health of our community.”
No appointment is necessary. Walk-ins are welcome during the following hours:
Monday through Wednesday: 8:30 a.m.-11 a.m. and 12:30 p.m.- 3:00 p.m. Thursday: 12:30 p.m.-3 p.m. PATH will provide:
Access to sterile supplies to reduce the spread of HIV, hepatitis C, and other infections Safe disposal of used supplies Overdose prevention education and free naloxone HIV and hepatitis C testing and linkage to treatment Referrals to substance use treatment, medical care, mental health services, and social support resources Education on safer use, wound care, and general health topics The Portsmouth Health Department stated its commitment to ensure that PATH operates as a welcoming, confidential, and non-judgmental space for all community members seeking support.
The program aligns with the Virginia Department of Health’s mission to protect health and also promote a well-being for everyone in the Commonwealth.
